title.zh: 卷二百五十六 列傳第一百四十四 崔景榮 黃克纘 畢自嚴 李長庚 劉之鳳
title.en: Volume 256 Biographies 144: Cui Jingrong, Huang Kezuan, Bi Ziyan, Li Zhanggeng, Liu Zhifeng
title.raw: 卷二百五十六 列傳第一百四十四 崔景榮 黃克纘 畢自嚴 李長庚 劉之鳳 Volume 256 Biographies 144: Cui Jingrong, Huang Kezuan, Bi Ziyan, Li Zhanggeng, Liu Zhifeng

sentences.zh: 崔景榮黃克纘畢自嚴李長庚

translations.literal: Cui Jingrong, Huang Kezuan, Bi Ziyan, Li Zhanggeng
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jingrong, Huang Kezuan, Bi Ziyan, and Li Zhanggeng

sentences.zh: （王誌道）〉

translations.literal: (Wang Zhidao)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Sub-biography: Wang Zhidao)]

sentences.zh: 劉之鳳

translations.literal: Liu Zhifeng
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhifeng

sentences.zh: 崔景榮，字自強，長垣人。

translations.literal: Cui Jingrong, courtesy name Ziqiang, was a native of Changyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jingrong, styled Ziqiang, came from Changyuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eleventh year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授平陽府推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Pingyang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed as the investigating censor for Pingyang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢御史，劾東廠太監張鯨罪。

translations.literal: He was promoted to censor and impeached Zhang Jing, eunuch of the Eastern Depot, for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to censor, he impeached Zhang Jing, the Eastern Depot eunuch, for criminal conduct.

sentences.zh: 巡按甘肅、湖廣、河南，最後按四川，積臺資十八年。

translations.literal: He toured and investigated in Gansu, Huguang, and Henan, and finally in Sichuan, accumulating eighteen years of censorial service.
translations.idiomatic: He served as touring investigating censor in Gansu, Huguang, and Henan, and finally in Sichuan, amassing eighteen years on the censorial bench.

sentences.zh: 播州亂，景榮監大帥遇劉綎、吳廣輩軍。

translations.literal: When the Bozhou rebellion broke out, Jingrong supervised the armies of the supreme commander Liu Ting, Wu Guang, and their fellows.
translations.idiomatic: During the Bozhou rebellion, Jingrong oversaw the forces of the supreme commander Liu Ting, Wu Guang, and their colleagues.

sentences.zh: 綎馳金帛至景榮家，為其父壽，景榮上疏劾之。

translations.literal: Ting sent gold and silks in haste to Jingrong's home as a birthday gift for his father; Jingrong memorialized the throne to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Ting hurried gold and silks to Jingrong's home as a birthday gift for his father; Jingrong memorialized the throne to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 播州平，或請以播北畀安氏，景榮不可。

translations.literal: After Bozhou was pacified, some asked to grant northern Bozhou to the An clan; Jingrong would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Once Bozhou was pacified, some proposed granting northern Bozhou to the An clan; Jingrong refused.

sentences.zh: 會總督李化龍憂去，景榮為請蠲蜀一歲租，恤上東五路，罷礦使。

translations.literal: When Grand Coordinator Li Hualong left on account of bereavement, Jingrong petitioned to remit one year's land tax in Sichuan, provide relief to the five routes of eastern Shang, and abolish the mining commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Grand Coordinator Li Hualong stepped down to observe mourning, Jingrong petitioned to remit one year's land tax in Sichuan, provide relief to the five eastern Shang routes, and abolish the mining commissioner.

sentences.zh: 化龍疏敘監軍功，弗及景榮。

translations.literal: In his memorial recounting merits from supervising the army, Hualong did not mention Jingrong.
translations.idiomatic: In his memorial on merits earned while supervising the army, Hualong made no mention of Jingrong.

sentences.zh: 已，晉太仆少卿。

translations.literal: Later he was promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was later promoted to Vice Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 三年滿，擢右僉都御史，巡撫寧夏。

translations.literal: At the end of three years he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: When his three-year term ended, he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 銀定素驕，歲入掠。

translations.literal: Yinding had long been arrogant and raided inward every year.
translations.idiomatic: Yinding had long been arrogant and launched raids into the interior every year.

sentences.zh: 景榮親督戰破之，因議革導賊諸部賞，諸部懼，請與銀定絕。

translations.literal: Jingrong personally directed the campaign and defeated him; he then proposed abolishing the rewards to the tribes that guided the bandits. The tribes were afraid and asked to break with Yinding.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong personally directed the fighting and defeated him; he then proposed abolishing the rewards paid to tribes that guided the raiders. The tribes, alarmed, asked to sever ties with Yinding.

sentences.zh: 銀定既失導，亦叩關求市。

translations.literal: Once Yinding had lost his guides, he too came to the passes seeking trade.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of his guides, Yinding too came to the border passes seeking trade.

sentences.zh: 寧夏歲市費不貲，景榮議省之。

translations.literal: Ningxia's annual trade fairs cost an enormous sum; Jingrong proposed reducing them.
translations.idiomatic: Ningxia's annual border markets cost a fortune; Jingrong proposed cutting them back.

sentences.zh: 在任三年，僅一市而已。

translations.literal: In three years in office there was only one fair.
translations.idiomatic: In three years in office he held only a single market.

sentences.zh: 其後延鎮吉能等挾款求補市，卒勿許，歲省金錢十余萬。

translations.literal: Later Yan, Zhen, Jineng, and others leveraged their good faith to demand restoration of the fairs; he ultimately refused, saving more than a hundred thousand in gold and silver each year.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan, Zhen, Jineng, and others used their record of compliance to demand the markets be restored; he ultimately refused, saving more than a hundred thousand taels of gold and silver annually.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，入為兵部右侍郎，總京營戎政。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year he entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of War and took charge of military administration for the capital garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year he entered the capital as Right Vice Minister of War and took charge of the capital garrisons' military administration.

sentences.zh: 改吏部，以疾辭去。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel but resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the Ministry of Personnel, he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 逾年，起宣府大同總督。

translations.literal: A year later he was recalled as Governor-General of Xuanfu and Datong.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled to serve as Governor-General of Xuanfu and Datong.

sentences.zh: 召還，晉兵部尚書。

translations.literal: He was recalled to the capital and promoted to Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to the capital, he was promoted to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 會遼、瀋失，熊廷弼、王化貞議不協，命廷臣議經、撫去留，景榮數為言官所論。

translations.literal: When Liaodong and Shenyang fell, Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen could not agree in counsel; the court was ordered to debate the retention or dismissal of the military governor and grand coordinator. Jingrong came under repeated attack from censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Liaodong and Shenyang were lost, Xiong Tingbi and Wang Huazhen could not reconcile their views; the court ordered a debate on whether to keep or dismiss the military governor and grand coordinator. Jingrong was repeatedly attacked by censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 御史方震孺請罷景榮，以孫承宗代之。

translations.literal: Censor Fang Zhenru asked that Jingrong be dismissed and replaced by Sun Chengzong.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fang Zhenru petitioned to dismiss Jingrong and replace him with Sun Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: He thereupon pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年十一月，特起為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Tianqi he was specially summoned to serve as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Tianqi he was specially summoned from retirement to serve as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 當是時，魏忠賢盜國柄，群小更相倚附，逐尚書趙南星。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Zhongxian usurped state power; his partisans relied on one another in turn and drove out Minister Zhao Nanxing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Zhongxian had seized control of the state; his factional hangers-on backed one another in turn and drove out Minister Zhao Nanxing.

sentences.zh: 即家起景榮，欲倚為助。

translations.literal: Jingrong was raised from retirement at home; they wished to rely on him for support.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong was summoned from his home; they meant to lean on him for support.

sentences.zh: 比至，忠賢飾大宅以待，景榮不赴。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Zhongxian had furnished a great mansion in readiness; Jingrong did not go to it.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, Zhongxian had prepared a lavish mansion for him; Jingrong did not accept it.

sentences.zh: 錦衣帥田爾耕來謁，又辭不見。

translations.literal: Tian Ergeng, commander of the Brocade-Clad Guard, came to pay his respects; he again declined to receive him.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Ergeng, commander of the Brocade-Clad Guard, came to call on him; he again refused to see him.

sentences.zh: 帝幸太學，忠賢欲先一日聽祭酒講，議裁諸聽講大臣賜坐賜茶禮，又議減考選員額，汰京堂添註官。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited the Imperial Academy, Zhongxian wished to listen to the chancellor lecture one day in advance; he proposed curtailing the ceremony of seats and tea for listening ministers, and also proposed reducing examination and selection quotas and eliminating supernumerary appointments at the capital ministries.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Imperial Academy, Zhongxian wished to hear the chancellor lecture a day early; he proposed cutting back the seating and tea ceremonies for ministers in attendance, and also proposed reducing examination quotas and purging supernumerary appointments at the capital ministries.

sentences.zh: 景榮皆力持不行，浸忤忠賢指。

translations.literal: Jingrong firmly resisted all of these on every point, gradually running counter to Zhongxian's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Jingrong firmly blocked every one of these measures, gradually falling afoul of Zhongxian's designs.

sentences.zh: 又移書魏廣微，勸其申救楊漣、左光鬥。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter to Wei Guangwei urging him to plead for Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Wei Guangwei urging him to intervene on behalf of Yang Lian and Zuo Guangdou.

sentences.zh: 廣微不得已，為具揭。

translations.literal: Guangwei had no choice but to draft a memorial on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwei, left no alternative, drafted a memorial on their behalf.

sentences.zh: 尋以景榮書為征，曰：「景榮教我也。

translations.literal: Soon Zhongxian took Jingrong's letter as evidence, saying, "Jingrong told me to do it."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhongxian seized on Jingrong's letter as proof, saying, "Jingrong put me up to it."

sentences.zh: 」於是御史倪文煥、門克新先後劾景榮陰護東林，媚奸邪而邀後福。

translations.literal: Thereupon censors Ni Wenhuan and Men Kexin successively impeached Jingrong for secretly shielding the Eastern Forest faction, flattering the wicked, and courting future reward.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon censors Ni Wenhuan and Men Kexin successively impeached Jingrong for secretly shielding the Eastern Forest faction, currying favor with the wicked, and angling for future reward.

sentences.zh: 得旨，削奪為民。

translations.literal: An imperial order followed stripping him of rank and reducing him to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order followed stripping him of rank and reducing him to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，復原職。

translations.literal: When Chongzhen assumed the throne his original office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongzhen took the throne, his original office was restored.

sentences.zh: 四年卒，贈少保。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year and was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year and was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 黃克纘，字紹夫，晉江人。

translations.literal: Huang Kezuan, courtesy name Shaofu, was a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Kezuan, styled Shaofu, came from Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷八年進士。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除壽州知州，入為刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed prefect of Shouzhou and later entered the Ministry of Justice as an assistant department director.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed prefect of Shouzhou, he later entered the Ministry of Justice as an assistant department director.

sentences.zh: 累官山東左布政使，就遷右副都御史，巡撫其地。

translations.literal: He rose through offices to Left Administrative Commissioner of Shandong, and was then promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made grand coordinator of that province.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to Left Administrative Commissioner of Shandong, then was promoted in place to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed grand coordinator of the province.

sentences.zh: 請停礦稅，論劾稅使陳增、馬堂，他惠政甚著。

translations.literal: He petitioned to halt mining taxes and memorialized against the tax commissioners Chen Zeng and Ma Tang; his other benevolent policies were very notable.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to halt mining taxes and impeached the tax commissioners Chen Zeng and Ma Tang; his other benevolent policies won wide notice.

sentences.zh: 屢以平盜功，加至兵部尚書。

translations.literal: Repeatedly rewarded for suppressing bandits, he was promoted as far as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Rewarded repeatedly for suppressing bandits, he was promoted all the way to Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 四十年，詔以故官參贊南京機務，為御史李若星、魏雲中所劾，還家候命。

translations.literal: In the fortieth year he was ordered to assist in Nanjing military affairs in his former capacity; censors Li Ruoxing and Wei Yunzhong impeached him, and he returned home to await orders.
translations.idiomatic: In the fortieth year he was ordered to assist in Nanjing military affairs at his former rank; impeached by censors Li Ruoxing and Wei Yunzhong, he returned home to await the emperor's decision.

sentences.zh: 居三年，始履任。

translations.literal: After three years at home he finally took up his post.
translations.idiomatic: After three years at home he finally assumed his duties.

sentences.zh: 四十四年冬，隆德殿災，上疏陳時政，語極痛切。

translations.literal: In the winter of the forty-fourth year, when Longde Hall burned, he memorialized on current affairs in language of extreme severity.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the forty-fourth year, after Longde Hall burned, he memorialized on current affairs in language of searing bluntness.

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no reply.

sentences.zh: 召理京營戎政，改刑部尚書，預受兩朝顧命。

translations.literal: He was summoned to take charge of military administration for the capital garrisons, transferred to Minister of Justice, and received the deathbed trusts of two reigns.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to oversee the capital garrisons' military administration, he was transferred to Minister of Justice and received the deathbed trusts of two reigns.

sentences.zh: 李選侍將移宮，其內侍王永福、姚進忠等八人坐盜乾清宮珠寶下吏。

translations.literal: When Lady Li was about to leave the palace, eight of her eunuchs—Wang Yongfu, Yao Jinzhong, and others—were charged with stealing jewels from the Palace of Heavenly Purity and handed over to the judicial authorities.
translations.idiomatic: As Lady Li was about to move out of the palace, eight of her eunuchs—Wang Yongfu, Yao Jinzhong, and others—were charged with stealing jewels from the Palace of Heavenly Purity and handed over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 克纘擬二人辟，余俱末減。

translations.literal: Kezuan proposed execution for two of them and reduced sentences for the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan proposed the death penalty for two of them and reduced sentences for the rest.

sentences.zh: 帝不從，命辟六人，余遣戍。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree and ordered six executed; the rest were sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused and ordered six executed; the rest were banished to frontier service.

sentences.zh: 克纘言：「姜升、鄭穩山、劉尚理不持一物，劉遜拾地上珠，還之選侍，而與永福、進忠同戮，輕重失倫。

translations.literal: Kezuan said: "Jiang Sheng, Zheng Wenshan, and Liu Shangli took not a single thing; Liu Xun picked up a pearl from the ground and returned it to Lady Li, yet they are to be executed together with Yongfu and Jinzhong—the gradation of punishment is out of balance."
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan said, "Jiang Sheng, Zheng Wenshan, and Liu Shangli took nothing at all; Liu Xun picked up a pearl from the floor and returned it to Lady Li, yet they are to die alongside Yongfu and Jinzhong—the gradation of punishment is out of balance."

sentences.zh: 況選侍篋中物，安知非先朝所賜？

translations.literal: Moreover, who is to say the items in Lady Li's casket were not gifts from the previous reign?"
translations.idiomatic: Besides, who can say the items in Lady Li's casket were not gifts from the previous reign?"

sentences.zh: 」當是時，諸珰罪重，謀脫無自，惟請帝厚待選侍，則獄情自緩。

translations.literal: At that time the eunuchs' crimes were grave and they had no way to escape on their own; they could only ask that the emperor treat Lady Li generously, and then the severity of the case would ease of itself.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the eunuchs' crimes were grave and they had no way to save themselves; they could only urge the emperor to treat Lady Li generously, in hopes the case would soften on its own.

sentences.zh: 於是流言四布，謂帝薄待先朝妃嬪，而克纘首入其言。

translations.literal: Rumors then spread everywhere that the emperor was treating the late emperor's consorts harshly, and that Kezuan was the first to give voice to this view.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors then spread that the emperor was treating the late emperor's consorts harshly, and that Kezuan had been the first to give voice to that view.

sentences.zh: 帝不悅，責克纘偏聽，命如前旨。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased, rebuked Kezuan for partial listening, and ordered that the previous edict stand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased, rebuked Kezuan for partiality, and ordered that the previous edict stand.

sentences.zh: 已，楊漣陳「移宮」始末。

translations.literal: Later Yang Lian set forth the full course of the Palace Transfer affair.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yang Lian laid out the full course of the Palace Transfer affair.

sentences.zh: 帝即宣諭廷臣，備述選侍淩虐聖母狀。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately announced to the court ministers a full account of how Lady Li had abused the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately announced to the court a full account of how Lady Li had abused the empress dowager.

sentences.zh: 且曰：「大小臣工，惟私李黨，責備朕躬。

translations.literal: He also said: "Ministers high and low think only of the Li faction's private interests and reproach my person."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Ministers high and low think only of the Li faction's private interests and reproach me personally."

sentences.zh: 」克纘皇恐上言：「禮，父母並尊。

translations.literal: Kezuan, in terror, memorialized: "By ritual, both parents are to be honored alike."
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan, in terror, memorialized, "By ritual, both parents are to be honored alike."

sentences.zh: 事有出於念母之誠，跡或涉於彰父之過，必委曲周全，渾然無跡，斯為大孝。

translations.literal: Matters that arise from sincere devotion to one's mother may in appearance touch on exposing one's father's faults; one must handle them with tact so that no trace remains—only this is great filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Acts born of sincere devotion to one's mother may in appearance touch on exposing one's father's faults; they must be handled with tact so that no trace remains—only this is great filial piety.

sentences.zh: 若謂黨庇李氏，責備聖躬，臣萬死不敢出。

translations.literal: If I am said to shield the Li faction by party and reproach the sacred person, I would not dare utter such words though I deserved ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: If I am accused of shielding the Li faction and reproaching Your Majesty, I would not dare utter such words though I deserved ten thousand deaths.

sentences.zh: 」御史焦源溥力駁其持論之謬，末言：「群豎持貲百萬，借安選侍為名，妄希脫罪，克纘墮其術而不覺。

translations.literal: Censor Jiao Yuanpu forcefully refuted the error of his position, concluding: "The eunuch clique holds a million in funds; under the pretext of securing Lady Li's welfare they vainly hope to escape punishment, and Kezuan has fallen for their trick without realizing it."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Jiao Yuanpu forcefully refuted the error of his position, concluding, "The eunuch clique holds a fortune in funds; under the pretext of securing Lady Li's welfare they vainly hope to escape punishment, and Kezuan has fallen for their trick without realizing it."

sentences.zh: 」克纘奏辨，因乞罷。

translations.literal: Kezuan memorialized in defense and asked to be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan memorialized in defense and asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 略言：「源溥謂在神宗時為元子者為忠，為福藩者非忠。

translations.literal: He said in brief: "Yuanpu holds that in the Shenzong era to support the heir apparent was loyal and to support the Prince of Fu was not loyal."
translations.idiomatic: He said in brief, "Yuanpu holds that in the Shenzong era to support the heir apparent was loyal and to support the Prince of Fu was not loyal."

sentences.zh: 臣敢廣之曰：神宗既保護先帝，授以大位，則為神考而全其貴妃，富貴其愛子者，尤忠之大也。

translations.literal: I venture to broaden this and say: since Shenzong protected the late emperor and invested him with the great throne, then to preserve his honored consort for the spirit of Shenzong and enrich his beloved son is loyalty of the highest order.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to broaden this and say: since Shenzong protected the late emperor and invested him with the great throne, then to preserve his honored consort for Shenzong's sake and enrich his beloved son is loyalty of the highest order.

sentences.zh: 又謂在先帝時為二後者為忠，為選侍者非忠。

translations.literal: He also holds that in the late emperor's era to support the two empresses was loyal and to support Lady Li was not loyal.
translations.idiomatic: He also holds that in the late emperor's era to support the two empresses was loyal and to support Lady Li was not loyal.

sentences.zh: 臣亦廣之曰：聖母既正名定位，則光昭刑於之令德，勿虛傳宮幃之忿爭，尤忠之大也。

translations.literal: I too broaden this and say: since the empress dowager has been given her rightful title and position, then to make manifest her exemplary virtue as a model to the realm and not spread idle tales of palace quarrels is likewise loyalty of the highest order.
translations.idiomatic: I broaden this as well: since the empress dowager has been given her rightful title and position, then to make manifest her exemplary virtue as a model to the realm and not spread idle tales of palace quarrels is likewise loyalty of the highest order.

sentences.zh: 若如源溥言，必先帝不得正其始，聖母不得正其終，方可議斯獄耳。

translations.literal: If Yuanpu's view is correct, only when the late emperor did not rightly begin and the empress dowager did not rightly end may this case be debated at all.
translations.idiomatic: If Yuanpu's view is correct, only when the late emperor did not rightly begin and the empress dowager did not rightly end may this case be debated at all.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，帝怒甚，責以輕肆無忌，不諳忠孝。

translations.literal: When the memorial entered, the emperor was greatly angered and rebuked him for levity, presumption, and ignorance of filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor was furious and rebuked him for levity, presumption, and ignorance of filial piety.

sentences.zh: 克纘皇恐引罪，大學士劉一燝等亦代為言，乃已。

translations.literal: Kezuan, in terror, acknowledged guilt; Grand Secretaries Liu Yijing and others also spoke on his behalf, and the matter ended.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan, in terror, acknowledged guilt; Grand Secretaries Liu Yijing and others also spoke on his behalf, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 無何，給事中董承業、孫傑、毛士龍，御史潘雲翼、楊新期，南京御史王允成並劾克纘是非舛謬。

translations.literal: Before long, supervising secretaries Dong Chengye, Sun Jie, and Mao Shilong, censors Pan Yunyi and Yang Xinqi, and Nanjing censor Wang Yuncheng jointly impeached Kezuan for confused and erroneous views.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, supervising secretaries Dong Chengye, Sun Jie, and Mao Shilong, censors Pan Yunyi and Yang Xinqi, and Nanjing censor Wang Yuncheng jointly impeached Kezuan for confused and erroneous views.

sentences.zh: 克纘不服，言曩不舉李三才，故為諸人所惡。

translations.literal: Kezuan would not accept this and said that because he had long refused to recommend Li Sancai, he was hated by these men.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan would not accept this and said that because he had long refused to recommend Li Sancai, he was hated by these men.

sentences.zh: 源溥復劾克纘借三才以傾言官。

translations.literal: Yuanpu again impeached Kezuan for using Sancai to undermine the censorial officials.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanpu again impeached Kezuan for using Sancai to undermine the censorial officials.

sentences.zh: 克纘奏辨，再乞休，帝不問。

translations.literal: Kezuan memorialized in defense and again asked to retire; the emperor took no notice.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan memorialized in defense and again asked to retire; the emperor took no notice.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年冬，加太子太保。

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Tianqi he was enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Tianqi he was enfeoffed as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 尋復以兵部尚書協理戎政。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Minister of War to assist in military administration.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again appointed Minister of War to assist in military administration.

sentences.zh: 廷臣議「紅丸」，克纘述進藥始末，力為方從哲辨。

translations.literal: When the court debated the Red Pill case, Kezuan recounted the course of administering the medicine and vigorously defended Fang Congzhe.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated the Red Pill case, Kezuan recounted how the medicine had been administered and vigorously defended Fang Congzhe.

sentences.zh: 給事中薛文周詆其滅倫常，昵私交，昧大義。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Xue Wenzhou denounced him for destroying moral order, clinging to private friendships, and ignoring great principle.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Xue Wenzhou denounced him for destroying moral order, clinging to private friendships, and ignoring great principle.

sentences.zh: 克纘憤，援《春秋》不書隱公、閔公之弒，力詆文周，且白選侍無毆聖母事。

translations.literal: Kezuan, indignant, cited that the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record the assassinations of Duke Yin and Duke Min, fiercely attacked Wenzhou, and also declared that Lady Li had not beaten the empress dowager to death.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan, indignant, cited that the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record the assassinations of Duke Yin and Duke Min, fiercely attacked Wenzhou, and also declared that Lady Li had not beaten the empress dowager to death.

sentences.zh: 給事中沈惟炳助文周復劾克纘。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Shen Weibing aided Wenzhou in again impeaching Kezuan.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Shen Weibing joined Wenzhou in again impeaching Kezuan.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝宣諭百官，明言選侍毆崩聖母。

translations.literal: Earlier the emperor had announced to all officials that Lady Li had beaten the empress dowager to death.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the emperor had announced to all officials that Lady Li had beaten the empress dowager to death.

sentences.zh: 及惟炳疏上，得旨：「選侍向有觸忤，朕一時傳諭，不無過激。

translations.literal: When Weibing's memorial went up, an imperial order came: "Lady Li had given offense in the past; my announcement at the time was not without excess."
translations.idiomatic: When Weibing's memorial went up, an imperial order came: "Lady Li had given offense in the past; my announcement at the time was not without excess."

sentences.zh: 追念皇考，豈能恝然？

translations.literal: When I recall my late father, how can I remain indifferent?"
translations.idiomatic: When I recall my late father, how can I remain indifferent?"

sentences.zh: 」於是外議紛紜，鹹言前此上諭，悉出王安矯托，而諸請安選侍者，益得藉為詞。

translations.literal: Public debate then swirled; all said the earlier imperial announcements had been forged at Wang An's instigation, and those who had petitioned to secure Lady Li's welfare gained further grounds for argument.
translations.idiomatic: Public debate then swirled; all said the earlier imperial announcements had been forged at Wang An's instigation, and those who had petitioned to secure Lady Li's welfare gained further grounds for argument.

sentences.zh: 蓋是時王安已死，魏忠賢方竊柄，故前後諭旨牴牾如此。

translations.literal: For by then Wang An was dead and Wei Zhongxian had just seized power, which is why the earlier and later edicts contradicted one another thus.
translations.idiomatic: For by then Wang An was dead and Wei Zhongxian had just seized power, which is why the earlier and later edicts contradicted one another so starkly.

sentences.zh: 克纘歷官中外，清強有執。

translations.literal: Kezuan served in offices at the capital and in the provinces; he was upright, forceful, and principled.
translations.idiomatic: Kezuan served at the capital and in the provinces; he was upright, forceful, and principled.

sentences.zh: 持議與爭「三案」者異，攻擊紛起。

translations.literal: His views differed from those who disputed the Three Cases, and attacks arose on every side.
translations.idiomatic: His views differed from those who disputed the Three Cases, and attacks arose on every side.

sentences.zh: 自是群小排東林，創《要典》，率推克纘為首功。

translations.literal: From this time the factional hangers-on drove out the Eastern Forest and compiled the Essentials Canon, generally crediting Kezuan with the leading merit.
translations.idiomatic: From this time the factional hangers-on drove out the Eastern Forest and compiled the Essentials Canon, generally crediting Kezuan with the leading merit.

sentences.zh: 時東林方盛，克纘移疾。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Forest was at its height, Kezuan pleaded illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Forest was at its height, Kezuan pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 詔加太子太傅，乘傳歸。

translations.literal: He was ordered enfeoffed as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and returned home by post-horse relay.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and returned home by post-horse relay.

sentences.zh: 四年十二月，魏忠賢盡逐東林，召克纘為工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the fourth year Wei Zhongxian drove out the Eastern Forest entirely and summoned Kezuan as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the fourth year Wei Zhongxian drove out the Eastern Forest entirely and summoned Kezuan as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 視事數月，復移疾歸。

translations.literal: After several months in office he again pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: After several months in office he again pleaded illness and returned home.

sentences.zh: 三殿成，加太子太師。

translations.literal: When the Three Halls were completed he was enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Halls were completed he was enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起南京吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled as Minister of Personnel in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was recalled to serve as Minister of Personnel in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 有劾之者，不就，卒於家。

translations.literal: Some impeached him; he did not take up the post and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: Impeached by others, he did not take up the post and died at home.

sentences.zh: 畢自嚴，字景曾，淄川人。

translations.literal: Bi Ziyan, courtesy name Jingzeng, was a native of Zichuan.
translations.idiomatic: Bi Ziyan, styled Jingzeng, came from Zichuan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十年進士。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twentieth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 除松江推官。

translations.literal: He was appointed investigating censor of Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed as the investigating censor for Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 年少有才幹，征授刑部主事。

translations.literal: Young and capable, he was summoned and made a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Young and capable, he was summoned to the capital and appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 歷工部員外郎中，遷淮徐道參議。

translations.literal: He served as an assistant department director in the Ministry of Works and was transferred to be administrative vice commissioner of the Huai-Xu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He served as an assistant department director in the Ministry of Works and was transferred to administrative vice commissioner of the Huai-Xu circuit.

sentences.zh: 內艱闋，分守冀寧。

translations.literal: When his period of mourning ended he was assigned to defend Jining in Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended he was assigned to defend Jining in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 改河東副使，引疾去。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be vice commissioner of Hedong and resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to vice commissioner of Hedong, he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 起洮岷兵備參政。

translations.literal: He was recalled as administrative commissioner for military preparedness in Tao and Min.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as administrative commissioner for military preparedness in the Tao-Min region.

sentences.zh: 以按察使徙治榆林西路，進右布政使。

translations.literal: As surveillance commissioner he was moved to administer the western route of Yulin and was promoted to Right Administrative Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As surveillance commissioner he was moved to administer the western route of Yulin and was promoted to Right Administrative Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 泰昌時，召為太仆卿。

translations.literal: In the Taichang era he was summoned as Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taichang era he was summoned to serve as Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年四月，遼陽覆。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi Liaoyang fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianqi Liaoyang fell.

sentences.zh: 廷議設天津巡撫，專飭海防，改自嚴右僉都御史以往。

translations.literal: The court debated establishing a grand coordinator at Tianjin to oversee coastal defense exclusively, and Ziyan was changed to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent there.
translations.idiomatic: The court debated establishing a Tianjin grand coordinator devoted to coastal defense, and Ziyan was appointed Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and sent there.

sentences.zh: 置水軍，繕戰艦，備戎器。

translations.literal: He established a naval force, repaired warships, and stocked military equipment.
translations.idiomatic: He established a naval force, repaired warships, and stocked military equipment.

sentences.zh: 及熊廷弼建三方布置策，天津居其一，增設鎮海諸營，用戚繼光遺法，水軍先習陸戰，軍由是可用。

translations.literal: When Xiong Tingbi devised the three-front disposition strategy, Tianjin was one of the three; additional camps such as Zhenhai were set up. Following Qi Jiguang's legacy methods, the navy first trained in land combat, and the army thereby became usable.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiong Tingbi devised the three-front disposition strategy, Tianjin was one of the three fronts; additional camps such as Zhenhai were established. Following Qi Jiguang's legacy methods, the navy trained first in land combat, and the force thereby became effective.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢令錦衣千戶劉僑逮天津廢將，自嚴以無駕帖疏論之，報聞。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian ordered Brocade-Clad Guard chiliarch Liu Qiao to arrest a dismissed general at Tianjin; Ziyan memorialized that there was no imperial warrant, and the court acknowledged receipt.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zhongxian ordered Brocade-Clad Guard chiliarch Liu Qiao to arrest a dismissed general at Tianjin; Ziyan memorialized that there was no imperial warrant, and the court acknowledged receipt.

sentences.zh: 四方所募兵日逃亡，用自嚴言，攝其親屬補伍。

translations.literal: Troops recruited from all quarters fled daily; adopting Ziyan's proposal, their kin were seized to fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Troops recruited from all quarters fled daily; adopting Ziyan's proposal, their relatives were seized to fill the ranks.

sentences.zh: 兵部主事來斯行有武略，自嚴請為監軍。

translations.literal: Lai Sixing, a principal secretary in the Ministry of War, was skilled in military affairs; Ziyan asked that he serve as supervising general.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Sixing, a principal secretary in the Ministry of War, was skilled in military affairs; Ziyan asked that he serve as supervising general.

sentences.zh: 山東白蓮妖賊起，令斯行率五千人往，功多。

translations.literal: White Lotus demon rebels rose in Shandong; he ordered Sixing to lead five thousand men there, with many achievements.
translations.idiomatic: White Lotus rebels rose in Shandong; he ordered Sixing to lead five thousand men there, with considerable success.

sentences.zh: 初，萬歷四十六年，遼左用兵，議行登、萊海運。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the forty-sixth year of Wanli, when troops were deployed in eastern Liaodong, sea transport via Deng and Lai was debated.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the forty-sixth year of Wanli, when troops were deployed in eastern Liaodong, sea transport via Dengzhou and Laizhou was debated.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，特設戶部侍郎一人，兼右僉都御史，出督遼餉，語詳《李長庚傳》。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially established, also holding Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, to go out and supervise Liaodong supplies; details are given in the biography of Li Zhanggeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially established, also holding Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, to go out and supervise Liaodong supplies; details are given in the biography of Li Zhanggeng.

sentences.zh: 及是，長庚遷，乃命自嚴代。

translations.literal: At this time Zhanggeng was transferred, and Ziyan was ordered to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: At this point Zhanggeng was transferred, and Ziyan was ordered to replace him.

sentences.zh: 敘前平賊功，進右都御史兼戶部左侍郎。

translations.literal: His earlier merit in suppressing rebels was recounted, and he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and Left Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Citing his earlier merit in suppressing rebels, he was promoted to Right Censor-in-Chief and Left Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時議省天津巡撫，令督餉侍郎兼領其事，即以委自嚴。

translations.literal: At the time it was debated to abolish the Tianjin grand coordinator and have the vice minister supervising supplies also take charge of that duty; this was entrusted to Ziyan.
translations.idiomatic: At the time it was debated to abolish the Tianjin grand coordinator and have the vice minister supervising supplies also take charge of that post; this was entrusted to Ziyan.

sentences.zh: 又議討朝鮮，自嚴言不可遽討，當俟請貢輸誠，東征效力，徐許其封耳。

translations.literal: There was also debate on attacking Korea; Ziyan said it could not be attacked hastily—one should wait until they requested tribute and showed sincerity, contributed to the eastern campaign, and only then slowly grant them investiture.
translations.idiomatic: There was also debate on attacking Korea; Ziyan argued that it could not be attacked hastily—one should wait until they requested tribute and showed sincerity, contributed to the eastern campaign, and only then slowly grant them investiture.

sentences.zh: 京師數地震，因言內批宜慎，恩澤宜節，人才宜惜，內操宜罷，語甚切直。

translations.literal: The capital suffered repeated earthquakes; he therefore said that inner rescripts should be cautious, favors restrained, talent cherished, and palace guards abolished—his language was very blunt.
translations.idiomatic: The capital suffered repeated earthquakes; he therefore urged caution in inner rescripts, restraint in imperial favors, care for talent, and abolition of palace guards—his language was blunt and direct.

sentences.zh: 自嚴在事數年，綜核撙節，公私賴之。

translations.literal: In several years in office Ziyan audited accounts and practiced economy; public and private affairs alike relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In several years in office Ziyan audited accounts and practiced economy; public and private affairs alike relied on him.

sentences.zh: 五年，以右都御史掌南京都察院。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made Right Censor-in-Chief and placed in charge of the Nanjing Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made Right Censor-in-Chief and placed in charge of the Nanjing Censorate.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，就改戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year he was transferred in place to Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year he was transferred in place to Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 忠賢議鬻南太仆牧馬草場，助殿工。

translations.literal: Zhongxian proposed selling the horse pastures of the Southern Court of the Imperial Stud to fund palace construction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian proposed selling the Southern Court of the Imperial Stud's horse pastures to fund palace construction.

sentences.zh: 自嚴持不可，遂引疾歸。

translations.literal: Ziyan held that this could not be done and thereupon pleaded illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan held that this could not be done and thereupon pleaded illness and retired.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，召拜戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 自嚴以度支大絀，請核逋賦，督屯田，嚴考成，汰冗卒，停薊、密、昌、永四鎮新增鹽菜銀二十二萬，俱報可。

translations.literal: Because revenue was greatly deficient, Ziyan asked to audit arrears in tax, supervise military colonies, enforce performance reviews, eliminate redundant soldiers, and halt the newly added salt-and-provisions silver of two hundred twenty thousand taels for the four garrisons of Ji, Mi, Chang, and Yong—all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: With revenue gravely short, Ziyan asked to audit tax arrears, supervise military colonies, enforce performance reviews, eliminate redundant soldiers, and halt the newly added salt-and-provisions payments of two hundred twenty thousand taels for the four garrisons of Ji, Mi, Chang, and Yong—all were approved.

sentences.zh: 二年三月，疏言：「諸邊年例，自遼餉外，為銀三百二十七萬八千有奇。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year he memorialized: "The annual quotas for the border garrisons, apart from Liaodong supplies, total more than 3,278,000 taels of silver."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the second year he memorialized, "The annual quotas for the border garrisons, apart from Liaodong supplies, total more than 3,278,000 taels of silver."

sentences.zh: 今薊、密諸鎮節省三十三萬，尚應二百九十四萬八千。

translations.literal: Now the Ji and Mi garrisons and others have saved three hundred thirty thousand; the amount still required is 2,948,000.
translations.idiomatic: With savings of three hundred thirty thousand from the Ji and Mi garrisons and others, the amount still required is 2,948,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 統計京邊歲入之數，田賦百六十九萬二千，鹽課百一十萬三千，關稅十六萬一千，雜稅十萬三千，事例約二十萬，凡三百二十六萬五千有奇。

translations.literal: Tallying the capital and border annual receipts: land tax 1,692,000, salt levy 1,103,000, customs duties 161,000, miscellaneous taxes 103,000, surcharges about 200,000—in all more than 3,265,000.
translations.idiomatic: Tallying annual receipts for the capital and borders: land tax 1,692,000, salt levy 1,103,000, customs 161,000, miscellaneous taxes 103,000, surcharges about 200,000—in all more than 3,265,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 而逋負相沿，所入不滿二百萬，即盡充邊餉，尚無贏余。

translations.literal: Yet arrears continued in succession; receipts did not reach two million—even if all were devoted to border supplies there would still be no surplus.
translations.idiomatic: Yet arrears persisted year after year; actual receipts fell short of two million—even if all were devoted to border supplies there would be no surplus.

sentences.zh: 乃京支雜項八十四萬，遼東提塘三十余萬，薊、遼撫賞十四萬，遼東舊餉改新餉二十萬，出浮於入，已一百十三萬六千。

translations.literal: Moreover capital miscellaneous expenditures were 840,000, Liaodong courier stations more than 300,000, Ji and Liaodong pacification gifts 140,000, and converting old Liaodong pay to new pay 200,000—expenditure already exceeded income by 1,136,000.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover capital miscellaneous expenditures totaled 840,000, Liaodong courier stations more than 300,000, Ji and Liaodong pacification gifts 140,000, and converting old Liaodong pay to new pay 200,000—expenditure already exceeded income by 1,136,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 況內供召買，宣、大撫賞，及一切不時之需，又有出常額外者。

translations.literal: Moreover there were inner-court procurements, Xuan and Datong pacification gifts, and all manner of extraordinary needs beyond the regular quotas.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover there were inner-court procurements, Xuan and Datong pacification gifts, and all manner of extraordinary needs beyond the regular quotas.

sentences.zh: 乞敕下廷臣，各陳所見。

translations.literal: I beg that Your Majesty order the court ministers each to state their views."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that Your Majesty order the court ministers each to state their views."

sentences.zh: 」於是廷臣爭效計畫。

translations.literal: Thereupon court ministers vied to offer plans.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon court ministers vied to offer plans.

sentences.zh: 自嚴擇其可者，先列上十二事，曰增鹽引，議鼓鑄，括雜稅，核隱田，稅寺產，核牙行，停修倉廒，止葺公署，南馬協濟，崇文鋪稅，京運撥兌，板木折價。

translations.literal: Ziyan selected what was feasible and first submitted twelve measures: increasing salt certificates, debating coin minting, collecting miscellaneous taxes, auditing concealed land, taxing monastery property, auditing broker houses, halting granary repairs, stopping office renovations, southern horses for mutual aid, Chongwen market taxes, capital transport allocation and exchange, and lumber price conversion.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan selected what was feasible and first submitted twelve measures: increasing salt certificates, debating coin minting, collecting miscellaneous taxes, auditing concealed land, taxing monastery property, auditing broker houses, halting granary repairs, stopping office renovations, southern horses for mutual aid, Chongwen market taxes, capital transport allocation and exchange, and lumber price conversion.

sentences.zh: 已，復列上十二事，曰增關稅，捐公費，鬻生祠，酌市稅，汰冗役，核虛冒，加抵贖，班軍折銀，吏胥納班，河濱灘蕩，京東水田，殿工冠帶。

translations.literal: Later he submitted another twelve: increasing customs duties, donating public funds, selling living shrines, adjusting market taxes, eliminating redundant labor, auditing false claims, increasing commutation fines, converting garrison troops to silver pay, clerks paying shift fees, riverbank shoals and marshes, eastern capital paddy fields, and palace-work honors and robes.
translations.idiomatic: Later he submitted another twelve: increasing customs duties, donating public funds, selling living shrines, adjusting market taxes, eliminating redundant labor, auditing false claims, increasing commutation fines, converting garrison troops to silver pay, clerks paying shift fees, riverbank shoals and marshes, eastern capital paddy fields, and palace-work honors and robes.

sentences.zh: 帝悉允行。

translations.literal: The emperor approved them all for implementation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved them all for implementation.

sentences.zh: 詔輯《賦役全書》。

translations.literal: An edict ordered compilation of the Complete Book of Taxes and Corvée.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered compilation of the Complete Book of Taxes and Corvée.

sentences.zh: 自嚴言：「《全書》之作，自行一條鞭始，距今已四十五年。

translations.literal: Ziyan said: "The compilation of the Complete Book began with the single-whip reform; it has now been forty-five years."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan said, "The compilation of the Complete Book began with the single-whip reform; it has now been forty-five years."

sentences.zh: 有一事而此多彼少者，其弊為混派；

translations.literal: When one item is assessed more here and less there, the abuse is called mixed apportionment;
translations.idiomatic: When one item is assessed more in one place and less in another, the abuse is called mixed apportionment;

sentences.zh: 有司聽奸吏暗灑瓜分，其弊為花派。

translations.literal: when officials let corrupt clerks secretly sprinkle and divide assessments, the abuse is called scattered apportionment.
translations.idiomatic: when officials let corrupt clerks secretly sprinkle and divide assessments, the abuse is called scattered apportionment.

sentences.zh: 當大為申飭。

translations.literal: These should be sternly prohibited.
translations.idiomatic: These should be sternly prohibited.

sentences.zh: 」因條八式以獻。

translations.literal: He thereupon set forth eight formulas and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon set forth eight formulas and presented them.

sentences.zh: 帝即命頒之天下。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately ordered them promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately ordered them promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 給事中汪始亨極論盜屯損餉之弊。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Wang Shiheng vigorously argued the harm of illegal military colonies draining supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Wang Shiheng vigorously argued the harm of illegal military colonies draining supplies.

sentences.zh: 自嚴言：「相沿已久，難於核實。

translations.literal: Ziyan said: "This has continued for a long time and is hard to verify in practice."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan said, "This has continued for a long time and is hard to verify in practice."

sentences.zh: 請無論軍種民種，一照民田起科。

translations.literal: I ask that whether military or civilian in origin, all be assessed alike according to civilian fields."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that whether military or civilian in origin, all be assessed alike according to civilian fields."

sentences.zh: 」帝是其議。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 先是，忠賢亂政，邊餉多缺，自嚴給發如期。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zhongxian threw the government into disorder, border supplies were often short; under Ziyan disbursements were made on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Zhongxian threw the government into disorder, border supplies were often short; under Ziyan disbursements were made on schedule.

sentences.zh: 又疏言：「最耗財者無如客餉。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Nothing drains funds like guest-pay."
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, "Nothing drains funds like guest-pay."

sentences.zh: 諸鎮年例合三百二十七萬，而客餉居三之一，宜大裁省。

translations.literal: The garrisons' annual quotas total 3,270,000, of which guest-pay accounts for one-third; it should be greatly cut.
translations.idiomatic: The garrisons' annual quotas total 3,270,000 taels, of which guest-pay accounts for one-third; it should be greatly reduced.

sentences.zh: 其次則有撫賞、召買、修築諸費，皆不可不節。

translations.literal: Next come pacification gifts, procurements, construction, and other expenses—all must be restrained."
translations.idiomatic: Next come pacification gifts, procurements, construction, and other expenses—all must be restrained."

sentences.zh: 」帝褒納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted this.

sentences.zh: 其冬，京師被兵，帝憂勞國事，旨中夜數發。

translations.literal: That winter the capital came under attack; the emperor, anxious over state affairs, issued edicts several times in the middle of the night.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the capital came under attack; the emperor, anxious over state affairs, issued edicts several times in the middle of the night.

sentences.zh: 自嚴奏答無滯，不敢安寢，頭目臃腫，事幸無乏。

translations.literal: Ziyan answered memorials without delay, dared not sleep peacefully, his head and eyes swelled, and affairs fortunately did not fail for want of supply.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan answered memorials without delay, dared not sleep peacefully, his head and eyes swelled from exhaustion, and affairs fortunately did not fail for want of supply.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，以六罪自劾，乞罷，優旨慰留。

translations.literal: The next summer he impeached himself on six counts and asked to be dismissed; a gracious edict comforted him and kept him in office.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer he impeached himself on six counts and asked to resign; a gracious edict comforted him and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 先以考滿加太子少保，敘遵、永克復功，再進太子太保。

translations.literal: Earlier, on completion of his term review he was enfeoffed as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; recounting the recovery of Zunhua and Yongping, he was further promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, on completion of his term review he was enfeoffed as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent; citing the recovery of Zunhua and Yongping, he was further promoted to Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書梁廷棟請增天下田賦，自嚴不能止。

translations.literal: Minister of War Liang Tingdong asked to increase land tax throughout the realm; Ziyan could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Liang Tingdong asked to increase land tax throughout the realm; Ziyan could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 於是舊增五百二十萬之外，更增百六十五萬有奇，天下益耗矣。

translations.literal: Thus beyond the previous increase of 5,200,000 there was a further increase of more than 1,650,000, and the realm grew still more exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Thus beyond the previous increase of 5,200,000 taels there was a further increase of more than 1,650,000, and the realm grew still more exhausted.

sentences.zh: 已，陳時務十事，意主利民，帝悉采納。

translations.literal: Later he set forth ten items on current affairs, aiming chiefly to benefit the people; the emperor adopted them all.
translations.idiomatic: Later he set forth ten items on current affairs, aiming chiefly to benefit the people; the emperor adopted them all.

sentences.zh: 又以兵餉日增，屢請清核，而兵部及督撫率為寢閣。

translations.literal: Because military pay grew daily, he repeatedly asked for a clear audit, but the Ministry of War and the governors generally shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Because military pay grew daily, he repeatedly asked for a clear audit, but the Ministry of War and the governors generally shelved the matter.

sentences.zh: 復乞汰內地無用之兵，帝即令嚴飭，然不能盡行也。

translations.literal: He again asked to eliminate useless troops in the interior; the emperor immediately ordered strict enforcement, yet it could not be fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to eliminate useless troops in the interior; the emperor immediately ordered strict enforcement, yet it could not be fully carried out.

sentences.zh: 御史余應桂劾自嚴殿試讀卷，首薦陳於泰，乃輔臣周延儒姻婭。

translations.literal: Censor Yu Yinggui impeached Ziyan for reading palace examination papers and ranking Chen Yutai first—Chen was a relative by marriage of Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yu Yinggui impeached Ziyan for reading palace examination papers and ranking Chen Yutai first—Chen was a relative by marriage of Grand Secretary Zhou Yanru.

sentences.zh: 自嚴引疾乞休，疏四上，不允。

translations.literal: Ziyan pleaded illness and asked to retire; he submitted four memorials and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan pleaded illness and asked to retire; he submitted four memorials and was not permitted.

sentences.zh: 時有詔，縣令將行取者，戶部先核其錢谷。

translations.literal: At the time there was an edict that for magistrates about to be selected for promotion, the Ministry of Revenue should first audit their grain and tax accounts.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was an edict that for magistrates about to be selected for promotion, the Ministry of Revenue should first audit their grain and tax accounts.

sentences.zh: 華亭知縣鄭友元已入為御史，先任青浦，逋金花銀二千九百。

translations.literal: Zheng Youyuan, magistrate of Huating, had already entered the capital as a censor; he had previously served in Qingpu and was in arrears on golden-flower silver by 2,900 taels.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Youyuan, magistrate of Huating, had already entered the capital as a censor; he had previously served in Qingpu and was in arrears on golden-flower silver by 2,900 taels.

sentences.zh: 帝以詰戶部，自嚴言友元已輸十之七貯太倉。

translations.literal: The emperor questioned the Ministry of Revenue; Ziyan said Youyuan had already paid seven-tenths, stored in the Grand Canal granary.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor questioned the Ministry of Revenue; Ziyan said Youyuan had already paid seven-tenths, stored in the Grand Canal granary.

sentences.zh: 帝令主庫者核實，無有，帝怒責自嚴。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the granary chief to verify; there was nothing; the emperor angrily rebuked Ziyan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the granary chief to verify; there was nothing; the emperor angrily rebuked Ziyan.

sentences.zh: 自嚴飾詞辨，帝益怒，遂下自嚴獄，遣使逮友元。

translations.literal: Ziyan argued with polished words; the emperor grew angrier, imprisoned Ziyan, and sent envoys to arrest Youyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyan argued with polished words; the emperor grew angrier, imprisoned Ziyan, and sent envoys to arrest Youyuan.

sentences.zh: 御史李若讜疏救，不納。

translations.literal: Censor Li Ruojian memorialized in his defense; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Ruojian memorialized in his defense; it was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 逾月，給事中吳甘來復抗疏論救，帝乃釋之。

translations.literal: After a month supervising secretary Wu Ganlai again submitted a forceful memorial in his defense, and the emperor then released him.
translations.idiomatic: After a month supervising secretary Wu Ganlai again submitted a forceful memorial in his defense, and the emperor then released him.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，敘四川平賊功，復官，致仕。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year his merit in pacifying rebels in Sichuan was recounted; his office was restored and he retired.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year his merit in pacifying rebels in Sichuan was recounted; his office was restored and he retired.

sentences.zh: 又三年卒，賜恤如制。

translations.literal: Three years later he died and was granted condolence gifts according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Three years later he died and was granted condolence gifts according to regulation.

sentences.zh: 李長庚，字酉卿，麻城人。

translations.literal: Li Zhanggeng, courtesy name Youqing, was a native of Macheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhanggeng, styled Youqing, came from Macheng.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十三年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-third year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 歷江西左、右布政使，所在勵清操。

translations.literal: He served as Left and Right Administrative Commissioner of Jiangxi, encouraging integrity wherever he was posted.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Left and Right Administrative Commissioner of Jiangxi, encouraging integrity wherever he was posted.

sentences.zh: 入為順天府尹。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as prefect of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as prefect of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 改右副都御史，巡撫山東。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and made Grand Coordinator of Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, he was appointed Grand Coordinator of Shandong.

sentences.zh: 盡心荒政，民賴以蘇。

translations.literal: He devoted himself to famine relief, and the people relied on him to recover.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to famine relief, and the people relied on him to recover.

sentences.zh: 盜蔓武定諸州縣，討擒其渠魁。

translations.literal: Bandits spread through Wuding and other prefectures and counties; he campaigned against them and captured their ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits spread through Wuding and other prefectures and counties; he campaigned against them and captured their ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，遼東用兵，議行登、萊海運。

translations.literal: In the forty-sixth year troops were deployed in Liaodong and sea transport via Deng and Lai was debated.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-sixth year troops were deployed in Liaodong and sea transport via Dengzhou and Laizhou was debated.

sentences.zh: 長庚初言不便，後言：「自登州望鐵山西北口，至羊頭凹，歷中島、長行島抵北信口，又歷兔兒島至深井，達蓋州，剝運一百二十里，抵娘娘宮，陸行至廣寧一百八十里，至遼陽一百六十里，每石費一金。

translations.literal: Zhanggeng at first said it was inconvenient, but later said: "From Dengzhou looking toward the northwest mouth of Tieshan to Yangtou'ao, passing Middle Island and Changxing Island to Beixin Mouth, then passing Rabbit Island to Shenjing and reaching Gaizhou—lighterage one hundred twenty li to Niangniang Palace; overland to Guangning one hundred eighty li, to Liaoyang one hundred sixty li—each shi costs one tael."
translations.idiomatic: Zhanggeng at first said it was impractical, but later said, "From Dengzhou toward the northwest mouth of Tieshan to Yangtou'ao, passing Middle Island and Changxing Island to Beixin Mouth, then Rabbit Island to Shenjing and Gaizhou—lighterage one hundred twenty li to Niangniang Palace; overland to Guangning one hundred eighty li, to Liaoyang one hundred sixty li—each shi of grain costs one tael."

sentences.zh: 」部議以為便，遂行之。

translations.literal: The ministry debated and deemed it convenient, and it was carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry debated and deemed it practical, and the route was adopted.

sentences.zh: 明年二月，特設戶部侍郎一人兼右僉都御史，出督遼餉，駐天津，即以長庚為之。

translations.literal: In the second month of the following year a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially established, also holding Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, to go out and supervise Liaodong supplies, stationed at Tianjin—and Zhanggeng was appointed to it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the following year a Vice Minister of Revenue was specially established, also holding Right Vice Censor-in-Chief, to supervise Liaodong supplies from Tianjin—and Zhanggeng was appointed.

sentences.zh: 奏行造淮船、通津路、議牛車、酌海道、截幫運、議錢法、設按臣、開事例、嚴海防九事。

translations.literal: He memorialized to implement nine measures: building Huai River ships, opening ferry routes, debating ox carts, assessing sea routes, cutting off escorted transport, debating currency law, establishing investigating censors, opening surcharge precedents, and tightening coastal defense.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to implement nine measures: building Huai River ships, opening ferry routes, debating ox carts, assessing sea routes, cutting off escorted transport, debating currency law, establishing investigating censors, opening surcharge precedents, and tightening coastal defense.

sentences.zh: 時議歲運米百八十萬石，豆九十萬石，草二千一百六十萬束，銀三百二十四萬兩，長庚請留金花，行改折，借稅課，言：「臣考會計錄，每歲本色、折色通計千四百六十一萬有奇。

translations.literal: At the time the annual transport was debated at 1,800,000 shi of rice, 900,000 shi of beans, 21,600,000 bundles of fodder, and 3,240,000 taels of silver. Zhanggeng asked to retain golden-flower silver, carry out commutation, and borrow tax levies, saying: "I have examined the accounting records: each year goods-in-kind and commuted payments together total more than 14,610,000."
translations.idiomatic: At the time annual transport was set at 1,800,000 shi of rice, 900,000 shi of beans, 21,600,000 bundles of fodder, and 3,240,000 taels of silver. Zhanggeng asked to retain golden-flower silver, carry out commutation, and borrow tax levies, saying, "I have examined the accounting records: each year goods-in-kind and commuted payments together total more than 14,610,000 taels."

sentences.zh: 入內府者六百余萬，入太倉者，自本色外，折色四百余萬。

translations.literal: What enters the inner palace exceeds six million; what enters the Grand Canal granary, apart from goods-in-kind, is more than four million in commuted payments.
translations.idiomatic: What enters the inner palace exceeds six million; what enters the Grand Canal granary, apart from goods-in-kind, is more than four million in commuted payments.

sentences.zh: 內府六百萬，自金花籽粒外，皆絲綿布帛蠟茶顏料之類，歲久皆朽敗。

translations.literal: The inner palace's six million, apart from golden-flower grain, consists of silks, cotton cloth, wax, tea, pigments, and the like—all rotting with age.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace's six million, apart from golden-flower grain, consists of silks, cotton cloth, wax, tea, pigments, and the like—all rotting with age.

sentences.zh: 若改折一年，無損於上，有益於下。

translations.literal: If commuted for one year, there would be no loss to the throne and benefit to the people.
translations.idiomatic: If commuted for one year, there would be no loss to the throne and benefit to the people.

sentences.zh: 他若陜西羊絨，江、浙織造，亦當稍停一年，濟軍國急。

translations.literal: Likewise Shaanxi lambswool and Jiang-Zhe weaving should also be paused for a year to meet the state's urgent military needs."
translations.idiomatic: Likewise Shaanxi lambswool and Jiang-Zhe weaving should also be paused for a year to meet the state's urgent military needs."

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅，言：「金花籽粒本祖宗舊制，內供正額及軍官月俸，所費不貲，安得借留？

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and said: "Golden-flower grain is the ancestral institution of our forefathers; the regular inner-court quota and officers' monthly pay cost an enormous sum—how can it be borrowed and retained?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and said, "Golden-flower grain is the ancestral institution of our forefathers; the regular inner-court quota and officers' monthly pay cost an enormous sum—how can it be borrowed and retained?"

sentences.zh: 其以今年天津、通州、江西、四川、廣西上供稅銀，盡充軍費。

translations.literal: Let this year's tribute silver from Tianjin, Tongzhou, Jiangxi, Sichuan, and Guangxi all be devoted to military expenses."
translations.idiomatic: Let this year's tribute silver from Tianjin, Tongzhou, Jiangxi, Sichuan, and Guangxi all be applied to military expenses."

sentences.zh: 」於是戶科給事中官應震上言：「考《會典》，於內庫則云：金花銀，國初解南京供武俸，諸邊或有急，亦取給其中。

translations.literal: Thereupon Revenue Section supervising secretary Guan Yingzhen memorialized: "Consulting the Collected Statutes, concerning the inner treasury it states: golden-flower silver—in the founding of the dynasty it was forwarded from Nanjing to pay military salaries, and when the borders had urgent needs it was also drawn from there."
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Revenue Section supervising secretary Guan Yingzhen memorialized, "Consulting the Collected Statutes, concerning the inner treasury it states: golden-flower silver—in the founding of the dynasty it was forwarded from Nanjing to pay military salaries, and when the borders had urgent needs it was also drawn from there."

sentences.zh: 正統元年，始自南京改解內庫。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhengtong it began to be redirected from Nanjing to the inner treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhengtong it began to be redirected from Nanjing to the inner treasury.

sentences.zh: 嗣後除武官俸外，皆為禦用。

translations.literal: Afterward, apart from military officers' pay, all was for imperial use.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, apart from military officers' pay, all was reserved for imperial use.

sentences.zh: 是金花銀國初常以濟邊，而正統後方供禦用也。

translations.literal: Thus golden-flower silver was commonly used to aid the borders at the founding, and only after Zhengtong was it devoted to imperial use.
translations.idiomatic: Thus golden-flower silver commonly aided the borders at the founding, and only after Zhengtong was it devoted to imperial use.

sentences.zh: 《會典》於太倉庫則云：嘉靖二十二年，題準諸處京運錢糧，不拘金花籽粒，應解內府者悉解貯太倉庫，備各邊應用。

translations.literal: The Collected Statutes concerning the Grand Canal granary state: in the twenty-second year of Jiajing it was approved that grain and funds transported to the capital from all places, whether golden-flower grain or not, that should have gone to the inner palace were all to be stored in the Grand Canal granary for use on the borders.
translations.idiomatic: The Collected Statutes concerning the Grand Canal granary state: in the twenty-second year of Jiajing it was approved that capital transport grain and funds from all places, whether golden-flower grain or not, that should have gone to the inner palace were all to be stored in the Grand Canal granary for use on the borders.

sentences.zh: 是世宗朝金花盡充兵餉，不知陛下初年何故斂之於內也。

translations.literal: Thus in the Shizong reign golden-flower funds were entirely devoted to military pay—one does not know why in Your Majesty's early years they were gathered into the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Thus in the Shizong reign golden-flower funds were entirely devoted to military pay—one wonders why in Your Majesty's early years they were gathered into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 今不考各邊取給應用之例，而反雲正供舊額，何相左若是？

translations.literal: Now without examining the precedents by which the borders drew supplies, you instead speak of the regular old quota—how can these be so opposed?
translations.idiomatic: Now without examining the precedents by which the borders drew supplies, you instead speak of the regular old quota—how can these be so contradictory?

sentences.zh: 至武官月俸，歲不過十余萬，乃雲所費不貲哉。

translations.literal: As for military officers' monthly pay, it is no more than a hundred thousand a year—how can you say the cost is enormous?
translations.idiomatic: As for military officers' monthly pay, it amounts to no more than a hundred thousand taels a year—how can you say the cost is enormous?

sentences.zh: 且原數一百萬，陛下始增二十萬，年深日久，顛末都忘。

translations.literal: Moreover the original sum was one million; Your Majesty first added two hundred thousand—with the years passing, the beginning and end have both been forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the original sum was one million; Your Majesty first added two hundred thousand—with the years passing, the whole story has been forgotten.

sentences.zh: 以臣計之，毋論今年當借，即嗣後年年借用可也；

translations.literal: In my reckoning, whether this year it should be borrowed or in succeeding years borrowed annually—all may be done;
translations.idiomatic: In my reckoning, whether this year it should be borrowed or in succeeding years borrowed annually—all may be done;

sentences.zh: 毋論未來者當濟邊，即見在內帑者盡還太倉可也。

translations.literal: whether future funds should aid the borders or what is now in the inner treasury should all be returned to the Grand Canal granary—that too may be done.
translations.idiomatic: whether future funds should aid the borders or what is now in the inner treasury should all be returned to the Grand Canal granary—that too may be done.

sentences.zh: 若夫物料改折，隆慶元年曾行之以解部濟邊，六年又行於南京監局，亦以濟邊。

translations.literal: As for commutation of materials, in the first year of Longqing it was once carried out to release ministry stores and aid the borders; in the sixth year it was again carried out at the Nanjing supervisory offices, likewise to aid the borders.
translations.idiomatic: As for commutation of materials, in the first year of Longqing it was carried out to release ministry stores and aid the borders; in the sixth year it was again carried out at the Nanjing supervisory offices, likewise to aid the borders.

sentences.zh: 此則祖宗舊制，陛下獨不聞耶？

translations.literal: These are the ancestral institutions—has Your Majesty alone not heard of them?"
translations.idiomatic: These are the ancestral institutions—has Your Majesty alone not heard of them?"

sentences.zh: 」帝卒不聽。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately refused to listen.

sentences.zh: 時諸事創始，百務坌集，長庚悉辦治。

translations.literal: At that time many undertakings were being launched and a hundred affairs piled up together; Zhanggeng handled them all.
translations.idiomatic: At that time many undertakings were being launched and affairs piled up on every side; Zhanggeng handled them all.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年，遷南京刑部尚書，就移戶部。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianqi he was transferred to Minister of Justice in Nanjing, then moved in place to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianqi he was transferred to Minister of Justice in Nanjing, then moved in place to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 明年，召拜戶部尚書，未任，以憂歸。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue but did not take office and returned home on account of bereavement.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was summoned and appointed Minister of Revenue but did not take office and returned home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 誌道，漳浦人，天啟時為給事中。

translations.literal: Zhidao was a native of Zhangpu and served as supervising secretary in the Tianqi era.
translations.idiomatic: Zhidao came from Zhangpu and served as supervising secretary in the Tianqi era.

sentences.zh: 議「三案」為高攀龍所駁，謝病歸。

translations.literal: His views on the Three Cases were refuted by Gao Panlong, and he resigned on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: His views on the Three Cases were refuted by Gao Panlong, and he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 其後附魏忠賢，歷擢左通政，論者薄之。

translations.literal: Later he attached himself to Wei Zhongxian and rose through posts to Left Commissioner of the Transmission Office; commentators held him in low esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Later he attached himself to Wei Zhongxian and rose through posts to Left Commissioner of the Transmission Office; commentators held him in low esteem.

sentences.zh: 及是，以忤中官罷。

translations.literal: At this time he was dismissed for offending a palace eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he was dismissed for offending a palace eunuch.

sentences.zh: 長庚不植黨援，與溫體仁不甚合。

translations.literal: Zhanggeng did not cultivate factional backing and did not get on well with Wen Tiren.
translations.idiomatic: Zhanggeng did not cultivate factional backing and was not on good terms with Wen Tiren.

sentences.zh: 推郎中王茂學為真定知府，帝不允。

translations.literal: He recommended Department Director Wang Maoxue as prefect of Zhending; the emperor did not approve.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Department Director Wang Maoxue as prefect of Zhending; the emperor did not approve.

sentences.zh: 復推為順德知府，帝怒，責以欺蒙，並追咎冠帶監生授職事，責令回奏。

translations.literal: He again recommended him as prefect of Shunde; the emperor was angry, rebuked him for deception, and also pursued blame for appointing students with honorary rank to office, ordering him to memorialize in reply.
translations.idiomatic: He again recommended him as prefect of Shunde; the emperor was angry, rebuked him for deception, and also pursued blame for appointing students with honorary rank to office, ordering him to memorialize in reply.

sentences.zh: 奏上，斥為民。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted he was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted he was stripped of rank and reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 家居十年，國變，久之卒。

translations.literal: He lived at home ten years; when the dynasty fell he died not long after.
translations.idiomatic: He lived at home ten years; when the dynasty fell he died not long after.

sentences.zh: 劉之鳳，字雍鳴，中牟人。

translations.literal: Liu Zhifeng, courtesy name Yongming, was a native of Zhongmou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhifeng, styled Yongming, came from Zhongmou.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-fourth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 歷南京御史。

translations.literal: He served as censor in Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a censor in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年六月，上疏別白孫承宗、王象乾、閻鳴泰本末，請定去留，而撤毛文龍海外軍，令居關內。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the third year of Tianqi he memorialized to clarify the full course of Sun Chengzong, Wang Xiangqian, and Yan Mingtai, asked to settle their retention or dismissal, and urged withdrawal of Mao Wenlong's overseas army to dwell inside the passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the third year of Tianqi he memorialized to clarify the full course of Sun Chengzong, Wang Xiangqian, and Yan Mingtai, asked to settle their retention or dismissal, and urged withdrawal of Mao Wenlong's overseas army to stations inside the passes.

sentences.zh: 又請亟罷內操。

translations.literal: He also asked that palace guards be abolished at once.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that palace guards be abolished at once.

sentences.zh: 忤魏忠賢，傳旨切責，復宣諭廷臣，再瀆奏者罪無赦。

translations.literal: Offending Wei Zhongxian, he received an edict of stern rebuke; the court ministers were again announced to that anyone who memorialized again would be punished without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Offending Wei Zhongxian, he received an edict of stern rebuke; the court ministers were again told that anyone who memorialized again would be punished without pardon.

sentences.zh: 六年，之鳳方視江防，期滿奏報。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Zhifeng was inspecting river defenses and, when his term ended, submitted his report.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Zhifeng was inspecting river defenses and, when his term ended, submitted his report.

sentences.zh: 忠賢奪其職。

translations.literal: Zhongxian stripped him of his post.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian stripped him of his post.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，起故官。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was recalled to his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chongzhen he was recalled to his former office.

sentences.zh: 帝召周延儒燕見，宵分始出。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned Zhou Yanru for a banquet audience; he did not leave until midnight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Zhou Yanru for a private audience over wine; he did not leave until midnight.

sentences.zh: 之鳳偕同官上疏曰：「臣等待罪陪京，去延儒原籍三百里，其立身居鄉，不堪置齒頰。

translations.literal: Zhifeng joined his colleagues in memorializing: "We await punishment while attending the capital, three hundred li from Yanru's native place; his conduct in office and at home is not fit to be mentioned."
translations.idiomatic: Zhifeng joined his colleagues in memorializing, "We await punishment while attending the capital, three hundred li from Yanru's native place; his conduct in office and at home is not fit to be mentioned."

sentences.zh: 今乃特蒙眷註，必將曰舉朝盡欺，獨延儒一人捐軀為國，使陛下真若廷臣無可信，而延儒乃得翦所忌，樹所私，曰為馮銓、霍維華等報怨。

translations.literal: Now he is specially favored; it will surely be said that the whole court deceives while Yanru alone gives his body for the state, making Your Majesty truly believe no court minister is trustworthy—whereupon Yanru can cut down those he resents, plant those he favors, and say he is avenging Feng Quan, Huo Weihua, and the like.
